items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: Bill Phillips and my brother and myself and Ruben McClendon was playing a banjo.

ctx.x: The Bienville Hotel. I think Stanley was playing piano. It was Billy's sister if I'm not mistaken, Bill Phillips and my brother and myself and Ruben McClendon was playing a banjo. We'll get him one night. I don't know where he lived. But he was playing banjo and he could play piano pretty good too. And we'd split every Sunday evening.
You say the Bienville Roof, did you play up on the roof? Yeah it was the Bienville Roof.

items.title: Bill Phillips Interview, 1961-05-24
items.q: Yeah, but we had a band before you went with that. Oh yeah, well yeah we had the Dejohn Phillips band. And we played at the lake together.

ctx.x: No, I started when I was quite a man. In 23 I started. I mean I started to practice it. But when I got out playing music it was around about 25. Because I went to the old man Cantrell for music lessons and reading lessons. And then after I went to Shalini. Old man Shalini, I went to him for about a year and a half or two years. And the first I went to Shalini and I wound up with Mr. Cantrell. And that's when, after I was there about two years, close to three years with him, then I went to Dejune's Orchestra. I…
Yeah, but we had a band before you went with that. Oh yeah, well yeah we had the Dejohn Phillips band. And we played at the lake together. At the lake together.

Millenburg, yeah with Willis-Darrisburg. And oh we played in a lot of places. That's what you get in there. We played at the Bamel apartment. We waked out on the boat. Which was on the lake or on the river?

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: So I tell you, that's why Deren's Boy, and Lewis Gallo, and Bill Phillips, that's why they hired me at the Japanese Tea Garden at Melon Boy

ctx.x: Just by yourself on clarinet, or?

Yeah, just by myself, just by myself. You can clarinet then? Yeah. Mm-hmm. I wasn't that great, but I mean, I could play that melody. You still need the blues. I could play that melody. Making that money, I could play that melody, you see. So I tell you, that's why Deren's Boy, and Lewis Gallo, and Bill Phillips, that's why they hired me at the Japanese Tea Garden at Melon Boy, because I could read them what I see. And they'd buy that music, and I'd read it for them, you see.
What was that Japanese tea garden like? Was it over the water, out in the camp?
